# Activation Clause

Maintains a document’s party roster, acceptance boundary and access guard. Business delivery depends on participant access, required acceptance of current terms and the document remaining open. Hosted bootstrap resolves account locators into authenticated transports before initialization. Executable hooks come from the admitted exact clause type.

## Configuration

Configuration is supplied through `parameters`; runtime state resides at `/activation` in the document where the clause executes.

- `parties` is a required, nonempty object keyed by party role. Each party requires `lead/channel`; optional `representatives` supplies representative IDs with their own `channel`. Transport names are the role and `role__representative`. Role and representative names must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`.
- `required` lists roles whose acceptance is needed and defaults to all initial party roles. An explicit empty list imposes no role-acceptance requirement, but cannot enable negotiation.
- `readerKeys` on parties and representatives supplies alternative keys for each reader group. `readers`, default `{}`, adds named groups; roster groups override identically named entries. Missing roster `readerKeys` becomes an empty group.
- `accessPaths`, default `[]`, identifies embedded Timeline Access documents. `/partyAccess` is also installed as an embedded collection for admission evidence.
- `allowNewParties`, default `false`, enables adding a new role through `updateParty`. `frozen`, default `false`, or `/partyRosterFrozen` equal to `true` initializes a frozen roster, blocking party updates and approved admissions.
- `revision` defaults to `1`. `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`; they allow specified deliveries before acceptance, subject to the access and closure checks below. Generated initial `approve_<role>` and `updateParty_<role>` operations are also allowed before acceptance.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths`, default `[]`, enables negotiation when nonempty. `admission/approvers` must be nonempty for the separate approved-admission function.

## Access and delivery

External Channel transports are exempt from Timeline Access matching. Every other transport must have the supported timeline-channel type and match at least one Timeline Access document containing its timeline, the same provider and at least one allowed key from **every** reader group. An empty required group cannot satisfy this check. Unsupported channels and incorrectly typed access documents fail validation.

Successful clause initialization and completed `Timeline Access Updated` events trigger refresh. Access updates are interpreted from the completed embedded document. Initial party transports remain pending until access is ready. When installed with a runtime timestamp, `/activation/channelsAdmittedAfter` records the cutoff: external deliveries at or before it are rejected.

The dispatch policy admits initialization refresh and registered embedded access-update deliveries before its other checks, allowing access recovery. Other deliveries require initialized activation state, `accessReady` equal to `true`, currently valid access and no `closed` flag. External operations listed for pre-activation, and non-external channels listed in `preActivationChannels`, may then run before acceptance. Other deliveries additionally require all required approvals and current terms.

A denied delivery skips every handler. External inputs are still consumed and checkpointed; they are not deferred or replayed when access or policy changes. Passing this policy does not override another installed policy or an operation’s own guards.

## Acceptance and state

`approve_<role>` runs on the party lead’s role channel, not its representative channels. It requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` equal to `true`, an input `revision` matching `/activation/revision`, and valid participant access. When negotiation is enabled, input `termsRef` is required text; whenever supplied, it must match `/activation/terms/ref`. Successful approval records `/activation/approved/<role>` and refreshes state. Repeated approval returns without recording another acceptance. One approval does not necessarily activate the document.

The runtime maintains:

- `parties`, `required`, `approved` and `revision`: the current roster, required accepting roles, recorded acceptances and roster/acceptance revision.
- `functional` and `accessReady`: the same computed access result. This includes proposed parties in pending `accessRequests` whose `expectedRevision` still matches, so pending admission can make access unavailable before roster admission.
- `termsAccepted`: all required roles have approved and document values still match `/activation/terms/fields`.
- `active`: access and acceptance are ready and the document is not closed. `everActivated` remains true after the first activation, even during later suspension.
- `status`: `CLOSED` takes precedence; otherwise unavailable access yields `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS` before first activation or `SUSPENDED_ACCESS` afterward. With access available, status is `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE` or `ACTIVE`.
- `reason`: `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED`, or an empty string. It does not independently describe closure.

These are maintained state values, not configuration defaults to infer when data is absent. Guard code treats missing required approvals as unapproved and missing `accessReady` as unavailable. Refresh records transitions for first activation, loss of access while active, and restored access leading back to active status. No operation for setting `closed` is established here.

`terms` contains a definition identity, agreed negotiable `fields` keyed by document path, and their combined `ref`; `termsRevision` starts at `1`. Initialization derives the definition identity from the initial document after removing configured access documents, activation `accessPaths` and `readers`, party-level `readerKeys`, and negotiable fields. Negotiable fields must exist and be text, integer, double or Boolean. Their live values must continue to equal the agreed values.

## Party changes and admission

`updateParty_<role>` requires exact-document review, a current party lead and an unfrozen roster. Input `party` defaults to the caller’s role; an existing different role cannot be managed. Input `replacement` supplies the complete replacement party, including `lead/channel`. Adding a role requires `allowNewParties`. Names, resulting access and contract-name conflicts are checked before installing roster contracts, incrementing `revision` and clearing all approvals. A newly added role is appended to `required`.

`Party Addition Requested` is a separate admission/access-preparation path. Its `parties` and `accessDocuments` carry the proposed roster information and native access histories keyed by transport name. Requests with stale `expectedRevision` or an already-recorded `admissionRef` are ignored. Valid requests install supplied public access histories, record `/activation/accessRequests`, and emit access requests for existing parties whose access does not cover the enlarged reader groups. Request `ready` values track observed access readiness; emitting a request neither grants private timeline access nor supplies participant consent.

The separate approved-admission function requires an unfrozen roster, matching `expectedRevision`, configured `admission/approvers`, main-party identity checks and valid resulting access. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; a changed roster installs contracts, increments `revision` and records admission events. This path does not itself append new roles to `required` or invariably clear approvals.

Whenever an established terms record exists and the roster or `required` changes, the terms identity and `termsRevision` change. Pending negotiation is closed as `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`; approvals are cleared when negotiation is enabled. Direct clause replacement is rejected in favor of party operations. While negotiation is configured and first activation has not occurred, changes to the clause set are also blocked.

## Negotiation

Nonempty `negotiation/allowedPaths` creates `proposeChanges_<role>`, `proposeAndActivate_<role>`, `activate_<role>`, `withdrawProposal_<role>`, `rejectProposal_<role>` and `withdrawAcceptance_<role>` for required roles. These require exact-document review and a caller channel present in the current `required` list.

Allowed paths must be unique absolute paths with nonempty segments and no `~`. They cannot begin with `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`, or equal or descend from a configured access path. Negotiation also requires the document’s `/type`; proposed documents must still match that type.

`proposeChanges` takes `proposalId`, matching `baseTermsRef`, and a nonempty `changes` list of `path` and `replacement` entries. Paths must be allowed and unique, replacement kinds must match current values, and terms must actually change. Replacing another pending proposal requires its ID in `supersedes`; closed proposal IDs cannot be reused. Recording a proposal does not apply its terms or establish acceptance.

`activate` requires `termsRef`. For current terms it delegates to ordinary approval and forbids `proposalId`. For proposed terms it requires the matching proposal ID and terms reference, revalidates the stored offer and records the caller’s approval through the inherited proposal mechanism. Only when that mechanism records completion are replacements applied, revisions advanced, approvals carried into activation state, negotiation made noneditable and the outcome recorded as `APPLIED`. `proposeAndActivate` combines proposing with that caller’s activation attempt; its name does not guarantee completion.

Before first activation, the proposer may withdraw a matching proposal, a required approver may reject it, and a required approver may withdraw their own acceptance of identified current or proposed terms. Proposal outcomes distinguish `WITHDRAWN`, `REJECTED`, `SUPERSEDED`, `AUTHORITY_CHANGED` and `APPLIED`. Activation of current terms closes a pending proposal as `SUPERSEDED`. Proposal creation, closure and acceptance withdrawal reject calls after `everActivated` becomes true.

The supplied definitions omit inherited admission/access-installation and proposal-completion helpers; their additional checks and exact completion rules are not established here.
